doc.title: Emile Barnes, George Guesnon, Little Brother Montgomery, Harold Dejan Interview, 1961-03-11

title: Guesnon's introduction to the tape and Louis James interview
summary: Guesnon introduces his informal tape of friends reminiscing, then briefly speaks with Louis James, who played in the 1927 Louis Dumaine band and played bass on a session with Herbert Morand.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Hello jazz lovers, this is Creole George Gaynor, veteran New Orleans Dixieland jazz band jurist and guitarist, saying hello. On this tape, which I call just reminiscing with friends, will be heard the actual voices of some of the greatest personalities in New Orleans jazz. Some singing, some playing, some just talking, but all for kicks and off the record. Such as little brother Montgomery, the great jazz piano man and composer of the great blues classic Vicksburg Blues, who also dropped in from Chicago just in time to join the party and left on this tape one of his new numbers, yet unrecorded, called the Satellite Blues. And again there is so many other little incidents that good friends recall when they get together to reminisce, and which I thought worthy of recording, as a memento of the gone but not forgotten good old days, and how it used to be when good friends got together. Here then is my first interview. And this is gonna be with one of the real old timers, way back from 1927 with the Louis Domains band, and this is Louis James. Well how are you Louis James? I'm fine, you know. I was right when I said you hadn't made another record since that time with a blowing instrument, is that right? Right. But you also made a recording session with my good friend Herbert Moran, but on that one you played bass, huh? That's right, that's right. Now, brother James, you and I are gonna sit down and do a little rehearsal, and what are we gonna play? We're gonna, just like I said, they got plenty of guys on you, what are we gonna put on you? It's gonna be for kicks. So let's tune up and have ourselves a ball. It's okay with me. Okay with you? Okay, okay. Alright. . . . ¶ 1961 with one of my good friends from Chicago, the one and only little brother Montgomery. Well, hello, little brother Montgomery, and how are you?
